samples.summary: Enforce-by-default flip leaves sibling design docs stating the opposite default, so the canonical docs now give two answers to "is the webhook enforcing?"
samples.evidence: This change makes enforcement the default (`isYorkieAuthEnforced`, yorkie-auth-webhook.md:30) and updates notes.md / slides-mobile.md / yorkie-auth-webhook.md — but not the other docs that build arguments on the old default: sharing.md:208 ("This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode" — the premise for calling the client-side gates load-bearing), revision-history.md:504-508, template-gallery.md:669, docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:300, and the index summary docs/design/README.md:155 ("shadow→enforce rollout"). The repo files docs by validity and folds into the canonical subsystem doc; leaving five docs asserting the inverse default is exactly the parallel-truth state that discipline exists to prevent.

samples.summary: A comment added by this very diff asserts the webhook "ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default", contradicting the default this same diff establishes
samples.evidence: The new extension comment in `initialize()` says "the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either", while the diff's own `readOnlyNoteStore` docstring (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:57-66) and notes.md:305-320 explicitly record that claim as *wrong*. The same stale claim survives untouched at packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40 and packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413, which are the docs-side twins this change is deliberately mirroring.

samples.summary: PDF role-based initialRoot is inlined instead of following the established `*InitialRootForRole` convention in `src/types/*-document.ts`
samples.evidence: `initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}` inlines the rule, while its own comment cites "Same rule as `docsInitialRootForRole` and its siblings". Those siblings are real, unit-tested helpers colocated with the root factory: `docsInitialRootForRole` (src/types/docs-document.ts:78), `boardInitialRootForRole` (board-document.ts:26), `notesInitialRootForRole` (notes-document.ts:67), `sheetsInitialRootForRole` (worksheet.ts), each with a `*-document.test.ts`. `initialPdfRoot` already lives at src/types/pdf-document.ts:14, so the reuse slot exists and was not used — the rule for pdf now lives at a different layer than for every other type.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` duplicates ~150 lines of security-relevant Proxy-trap machinery from `readOnlyDocStore` rather than sharing it
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts reproduces packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts nearly verbatim — the same memoized `get`, non-configurable-descriptor exception, `batch` passthrough, and the `set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`isExtensible`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` traps. Only the reader allowlist and the `undo`/`redo` return type genuinely differ, and those are parameters, not structure. Two copies of an access-control proxy will diverge: a trap fix or an invariant correction applied to one silently leaves the other behind. Mitigating context: shared-core-extraction.md:84 lists "Store abstraction" as a deferred Non-Goal (Tier C), and `@wafflebase/notes` does not currently depend on `@wafflebase/core` — so a generic `readOnlyProxy(readers, overrides)` in core, not a shared store interface, is what was available.

samples.summary: The read-only write-suppression sweep across sheets, pdf and board is not reflected in those subsystems' design docs, two of which now assert the opposite
samples.evidence: This change adds a `readOnly` write boundary to `YorkieStore` (presence seed, `updateSelection`, `ensureAxisOrder`, and throwing `assertWritable` on all five comment mutators), a `readOnly` prop to `CommentPopover`, a skipped seed in `pdf-collab`, and a presence gate in `board-view`. Only notes.md, slides-mobile.md and yorkie-auth-webhook.md were updated. sheets/comments.md:442 still states "The Yorkie backend already enforces read-only for anonymous; this design adds no new permission surface beyond Store calls", and pdf.md:206-208 still states the `comments` map is seeded at bootstrap and "never created lazily" — both now false for a viewer mount.

samples.summary: Share-link viewers now publish no presence at all on any document type — a user-visible product change not recorded in the doc that owns shared-mount presence
samples.evidence: Presence writes are suppressed for read-only mounts in board-view.tsx (selection), slides-view.tsx (`broadcast`), pdf-collab.tsx (`activePage`), yorkie-store.ts (`activeTabId` seed + `updateSelection`), yorkie-doc-store.ts (cursor/selection) and `readOnlyNoteStore` (`setLocalSelection`). The net effect is that a viewer becomes invisible to collaborators (no avatar cursor, no page/slide indicator). sharing.md:143-149 is where the shared layouts' presence identity behavior is documented ("Attempts to detect logged-in users for presence identity; falls back to Anonymous") and it was not updated; the trade-off is recorded only in scattered code comments.

samples.summary: The notes view-state trio and the mobile `both`→`edit` demotion rule are now implemented twice, in the workspace route and the new shared route
samples.evidence: `shared-notes-layout.tsx` re-implements what `notes-detail.tsx:90-138` already does: `viewMode`/`keymap`/`showAuthors` state seeded from `readViewMode`/`readKeymap`/`readShowAuthors`, `useIsMobile()`, and `isMobile && viewMode === 'both' ? 'edit' : viewMode`. notes.md now documents that demotion as one rule shared by "both mounting routes" (and notes-toolbar.tsx:402 was edited to say exactly that), but it lives in two places, so the two can drift. A small `useNotesViewState({ persist })` hook would have carried the persist/no-persist difference the doc calls out as the only intended divergence.

samples.summary: Two unrelated CI-flake fixes are bundled into an auth-hardening + notes-parity change
samples.evidence: The DuckDB extension-download warmup in lakehouse-parity.e2e-spec.ts and the jsdom editor-disposal cleanup in packages/docs/test/view/{large-paste-indicator,update-style-to-match}.test.ts share no subject with either the Yorkie enforce-by-default work or issue #1044's notes share-link toolbar. Both look correct and cheap, but they widen the blast radius of a change whose other half flips a deployment-wide security default.
